maximum_permitted_stay: Visitor permit valid 40 days; extension up to 30 additional days may be granted where justified.
entry_count: Not specified; permit cannot be amended.
passport_validity_rule: Passport valid for the entire permit duration plus at least four additional weeks.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count is published in GSGSSI visitor-permit guidance.
return_ticket_rule: No air return-ticket rule is published; vessel name and intended first arrival/departure dates are required. Access is by sea only.
proof_of_funds_rule: No separate minimum funds amount is published; the visitor permit fee and adequate health insurance are required.
accommodation_rule: No visitor accommodation ashore; visitors arrive by sea and require vessel-based support throughout the visit.
travel_insurance_rule: Adequate health insurance must cover emergency evacuation to a country with suitable treatment, transport and medical care in transit, and repatriation of remains.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: The visitor-permit guidance does not list a vaccination requirement; adequate health insurance is mandatory. There are no medical facilities for visitors.
transit_rule: Accessible only by sea. Vessel manifests must be validated and submitted at least 72 hours before arrival. Separate visas may be needed for the embarkation or transit country.
application_channel: ETA portal https://eta.entry.gov.gs (Chrome/Edge); individual or group via authorised agent, cruise/yacht operator or family. Check if operator applies.
application_fee: GBP 250 for a 40-day visitor permit from 1 July 2026; GBP 50 late fee within 8 days of arrival.
processing_time: No SLA; apply early. Within 14 days requires justification; within 8 days: GBP 50 late fee; within 3 days: no approval.

review_notes: GSGSSI is a British Overseas Territory. The Government states that from 1 August 2025 all persons entering for work or visitor purposes require an Entry Permit unless they fall within the narrow deemed-permission classes. The official policy lists Crown military/civil service, GSGSSI/British Antarctic Survey personnel, certain vessel crew and emergencies; ordinary tourists are not exempt. The rule is nationality-neutral and the application requires nationality to match the travel document, so a Bangladeshi ordinary-passport tourist must obtain the Visitor Entry Permit. This is not a visa: visa_required=false, but visa_free_eligibility=false because the permit is mandatory. Current fee is GBP 250 for 40 days from 1 July 2026. Apply through the electronic permit portal; applications made within 14 days are only accepted where earlier filing was impracticable, applications submitted or unpaid within 8 days incur a GBP 50 late fee, and applications within 3 days are not approved. A visitor permit may be extended by up to 30 days where justified, cannot be amended, and unused permits are not refunded. The territory is accessible only by sea, has no visitor accommodation ashore or medical facilities, and requires vessel-based support and adequate evacuation/repatriation insurance. Separate visas may be needed for the embarkation or transit country.
